description:
FILED s473 (Fable, 2026-09-06) from the companion `--all --quick` on main + serial re-runs on main d348dcea AND on a `git archive 637fc58e` extraction (both 129/12 -- PRE-EXISTING before BX; the snapshot row `op/tie_fetch_count.t 343 0 76 65` was stale: 55 `-X $tied_glob` / `-X` filetest rows had been FIXED earlier (the s470bs/s470bx filetest operand family) and these two had started failing).

THE ROWS (perl's t/op/tie_fetch_count.t lines 71-72; `check_count` asserts FETCH was called exactly once):
    @dummy = $v42 .. "a";   check_count '$tied.."a"';
    @dummy = "a"  .. $v42;   check_count '"a"..$tied';
The NUMERIC spellings (`$var .. 1`, `1 .. $var`, lines 68-69) PASS -- so the double read is in the range operator's MAGIC-STRING decision: perl decides "is this the string range or the numeric range" by `looks_like_number` on the ALREADY-FETCHED value; PCL reads the operand once for the decision and once more for the value.  Perl's rule (pp_flop): both operands are fetched ONCE, then `SvNIOKp || !SvPOKp || looks_like_number` decides.

FIX SHAPE: `p-range`/the list-range lowering evaluates each operand ONCE into a temp (a `let`) before the numeric/string decision -- one line in the runtime macro or the emitter; a tied-operand probe (a `tie` FETCH counter, the test's own shape) for `..` in list context with string/number/undef operands on either side, and the flip-flop (`..` in scalar context, sed-style) which must NOT change (probe perl: the flip-flop FETCHes its operand once per evaluation too).  Guard rows beside the range guards; companion op/tie_fetch_count.t 129/12 -> 131/10; snapshot spliced with this task as the cause.

=== DONE (s473h, Opus, 2026-09-08) ===
The fix shape was right; the LOCATION was one level out.  It is not `p-..`'s
numeric/string decision: it is %p-array-fill-range (the #1204 segment fill),
which classified the range with %p-range-classify and THEN called `p-..` for
the STRING arm -- and `p-..` classifies again.  %p-range-classify UNBOXES its
operands, and unboxing a tied scalar is a FETCH.  The numeric arm never had
the bug because it never called back into `p-..`, which is exactly why the
numeric spellings (rows 68-69) always passed.

FIX: the string-range builder is split out as %p-range-string-vector, taking
bounds ALREADY classified; both arms call it, so they cannot disagree again
(rule 11).  One function moved, two call sites.

PROBED with the test's own tie shape (scratch/s473h/probe/m8b.pl): all shapes
now match perl 5.40.3 -- `$tied.."a"` and `"a"..$tied` with a string value,
the numeric spellings, undef on either side, and `my @out = ($tied .. "c")`.
The scalar-context flip-flop (both `..` and `...`, and one with a tied
condition) and every string-range shape (`az`..`bb`, `A`..`C`, `e`..`a`,
`-x`..`-z`, a mid-list range, an `@arr =` range) are byte-identical to the
a9f2a264 extraction.

COMPANION op/tie_fetch_count.t 129/12 -> 131/10; the two FIXED ROWs are
exactly this task's ('$tied.."a"' and '"a"..$tied'); serial re-run agrees
(#366); 0 NEW ROW, and a confirmation run reads 0 NEW / 0 FIXED.  The
snapshot row (baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv) and the two removed rows in
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv were edited ROW BY ROW with the cause.

GUARDS: Pl/t/range-01.t 12 -> 18 (rows 13-14 and 16 fail on the a9f2a264
extraction; the flip-flop row and the string-range row are the negatives that
must keep passing).  Commit 41039d33.
